reasons: The regulation covers distance sellers of financial services and applies only to financial services contracts.
Your shop sells coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — food products — not financial services.
You are established in France and ship to all 27 EU countries, so the EU distance-selling rules cover your store.
You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate directly to consumers online, which are distance contracts that trigger a withdrawal right.
Your company is a medium-sized or large enterprise, so the 2026-06-19 effective date applies to you.

todos.text: Add the model withdrawal form, withdrawal conditions, time limits and procedures to your storefront
todos.quote: where a right of withdrawal exists, the conditions, time limit and procedures for exercising that right in accordance with Article 11(1), as well as the model withdrawal form set out in Annex I(B), and, where applicable, information about the existence and placement of the withdrawal function referred to in Article 11a;

todos.text: Display clear information about the existence and placement of the withdrawal function on your storefront
todos.quote: where a right of withdrawal exists, the conditions, time limit and procedures for exercising that right in accordance with Article 11(1), as well as the model withdrawal form set out in Annex I(B), and, where applicable, information about the existence and placement of the withdrawal function referred to in Article 11a;

reasons: You are established in France and ship to all EU countries, so the EU directive covers your shop.
You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate through a Shopify storefront, which is an online interface for distance contracts.
The obligations are addressed to the trader — that is you as the seller — and your company size (medium or large) falls under the single effective date given.

todos.text: Make sure the withdrawal function stays continuously available throughout the entire withdrawal period on your storefront
todos.quote: The withdrawal function shall be continuously available throughout the withdrawal period.

todos.text: Place the withdrawal function prominently on your online store so consumers can easily find and access it
todos.quote: It shall be prominently displayed on the online interface and easily accessible to the consumer.

todos.text: Set up the withdrawal function so consumers can submit an online withdrawal statement that captures their name, the contract details, and the electronic means for the confirmation
todos.quote: The withdrawal function shall enable the consumer to send an online withdrawal statement informing the trader of his or her decision to withdraw from the contract. That online withdrawal statement shall enable the consumer to easily provide or confirm the following information: (a)his or her name; (b)details identifying the contract from which he or she wishes to withdraw; (c)details of the electronic means by which the confirmation of the withdrawal will be sent to the consumer.

todos.text: After the consumer activates the confirmation function, automatically send an acknowledgement of receipt on a durable medium that includes the withdrawal content and the date and time of submission
todos.quote: Once the consumer activates the confirmation function, the trader shall send to the consumer an acknowledgement of receipt of the withdrawal on a durable medium, including its content and the date and time of its submission, without undue delay.

reasons: The regulation requires pre-contractual information for distance financial service contracts.
Your shop sells coffee, cocoa and chocolate — physical goods — not financial services.
Because the obligations only bind traders offering financial services, they do not apply to your business.
The regulation covers distance financial services such as consumer credit agreements concluded online.
Your shop sells coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — physical goods, not financial services.
Therefore the obligations about human intervention and burden of proof for adequate explanations do not bind you.
The regulation change requires Member States to set up penalty frameworks for distance financial service contracts.
Your shop sells coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — not financial services — and the obligation is addressed to national governments, not to retailers.
The obligation is addressed to Member States — national governments — not to individual sellers or shops.
Your shop is a private business selling coffee, cocoa and chocolate, not a government entity required to notify the Commission.
The regulation updates financial services contract rules for distance selling, but you sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — physical goods, not financial services.
The sole obligation directs member states to amend an annex of the Consumer Rights Directive, not sellers to change their practices.
The Directive addresses Member States' obligation to transpose rules for distance-selling financial services contracts into national law.
Your shop sells coffee, cocoa, and chocolate, not financial services.
The obligations are directed at national governments, not at product sellers.
You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate, which are listed relevant commodities under the EU Deforestation Regulation.
Your shop is established in France and imports these goods from outside the EU, so you are the operator placing them on the EU market.
As a medium-sized or large enterprise, the obligations bind you from the earlier effective date.

todos.text: Verify that your coffee, cocoa and chocolate supplies comply with the production country's laws
todos.quote: they have been produced in accordance with the relevant legislation of the country of production;

todos.text: Obtain or prepare a due diligence statement or simplified declaration for each coffee, cocoa and chocolate product you place on the market
todos.quote: they are covered by a due diligence statement or a simplified declaration, as required by the relevant provisions of this Regulation.

reasons: This applies because you are established in France, ship to all EU countries, and sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate — all listed as relevant products under the EU Deforestation Regulation.
Since you import these goods from outside the EU or produce them yourself, you are the operator placing them on the EU market for the first time.
Your company size is medium or large, so the non-SME obligations and the earlier effective date bind you.

todos.text: Before listing any coffee, cocoa or chocolate product, confirm you have the supplier and customer details required by the regulation.
todos.quote: Downstream operators and traders shall place or make available on the market or export relevant products only if they are in possession of the information required under paragraph 3.

todos.text: Set up a register to capture the name, address, email, website and any due-diligence reference for every supplier and every business customer of your coffee, cocoa and chocolate lines.
todos.quote: Downstream operators and traders shall collect and keep the following information relating to the relevant products they intend to place or make available on the market or export: (a) the name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, the postal address, the email address and, if available, a web address of the operators, downstream operators, or the traders who have supplied the relevant products to them, as well as, only in the event that their supplier is an operator, the reference numbers of the due diligence statements or the declaration identifiers associated to those products; (b) the name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, the postal address, the email address and, if available, a web address of the downstream operators, or the traders to whom they have supplied the relevant products.

todos.text: Create a five-year retention folder (digital or paper) for the supplier and customer records of each relevant product and be ready to hand it to authorities on request.
todos.quote: Downstream operators and traders shall keep the information referred to in paragraph 3 for at least five years from the date of the placing or making available on the market or export, and shall provide that information to the competent authorities upon request.

todos.text: Draft a one-page alert template so you can notify the competent authority in any EU country where you sell, plus your business customers, the moment you learn a product may not comply.
todos.quote: Downstream operators and traders that obtain or are made aware of relevant new information, including substantiated concerns, indicating that a relevant product that they have placed or made available on the market is at risk of not complying with this Regulation shall immediately inform the competent authorities of the Member States in which they placed or made available on the market the relevant product as well as downstream operators and traders to whom they supplied the relevant product. In the case of exports, downstream operators shall inform the competent authority of the Member State which is the country of production.

todos.text: Prepare a cooperation pack — product files, premises access notes, contact person — so you can respond quickly if an authority asks for an Article 19 check.
todos.quote: Downstream operators and traders shall offer all necessary assistance to the competent authorities to facilitate the carrying out of the checks under Article 19, including access to premises and the making available of documentation and records.

reasons: You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate, which are listed commodities under the EU Deforestation Regulation.
Your business is established in France and imports these goods from outside the EU, so you are an operator placing relevant products on the EU market.
As a medium-sized or large enterprise, the obligations take effect for you on 30 December 2026.

todos.text: Consider appointing an authorised representative to submit due diligence statements on your behalf
todos.quote: Operators may mandate an authorised representative to submit the due diligence statement pursuant to Article 4(2) or to submit a simplified declaration pursuant to Article 4a(2) on their behalf.

todos.text: Set up a due diligence process for all coffee, cocoa and chocolate products before placing them on the market
todos.quote: Prior to placing relevant products on the market or exporting them, operators shall exercise due diligence with regard to all relevant products.

todos.text: Start collecting the information, data and documents required under Article 9 for your coffee, cocoa and chocolate supply chains
todos.quote: the collection of information, data and documents needed to fulfil the requirements set out in Article 9;

todos.text: Implement risk assessment procedures for your coffee, cocoa and chocolate products as outlined in Article 10
todos.quote: risk assessment measures as referred to in Article 10;

todos.text: Prepare risk mitigation measures for any identified risks in your coffee, cocoa and chocolate supply chains per Article 11
todos.quote: risk mitigation measures as referred to in Article 11.

reasons: You sell coffee and cocoa products, which are covered by the EU Deforestation Regulation.
You are established in France and import these goods from outside the EU, making you an operator placing them on the EU market.
Your company size is medium or large, so the obligations bind you directly.

todos.text: Set up a system to store all required product information for five years and be ready to provide it to authorities on request
todos.quote: The operator shall make available to the competent authorities upon request the information, documents and data collected under this Article.

reasons: You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate, which are relevant products under the EU Deforestation Regulation.
You import these goods from outside the EU (or make them yourself), so you are the operator placing them on the EU market.
Your company is a medium-sized or large enterprise established in France and you ship to all EU countries.

todos.text: Conduct a risk assessment for each coffee, cocoa and chocolate product before you place it on the market or export it, and only proceed if the assessment shows no or negligible risk of non-compliance
todos.quote: Operators shall not place the relevant products on the market or export them, except where the risk assessment reveals no or only a negligible risk that the relevant products are non-compliant.

todos.text: Document every risk assessment and set a recurring annual review so each one is updated at least once a year
todos.quote: The operators shall document and review the risk assessments at least on an annual basis and make them available to the competent authorities upon request.

todos.text: Create a record that shows how you checked the information you gathered against the risk assessment criteria and how you concluded the degree of risk
todos.quote: Operators shall be able to demonstrate how the information gathered was checked against the risk assessment criteria set out in paragraph 2 and how they determined the degree of risk.

reasons: The obligations in Article 16 are addressed to competent authorities — government enforcement bodies — not to operators or traders like your shop.
Your shop sells coffee and cocoa and imports them from outside the EU, so the Regulation overall applies to you, but this specific article only tells authorities how to plan and carry out checks.
You are established in France and import coffee and cocoa from outside the EU, which makes you an operator placing relevant products on the EU market for the first time.
Coffee, cocoa, and chocolate (a cocoa-derived product) are listed commodities under the EU Deforestation Regulation, so your product range falls squarely inside its scope.
As a medium-sized or large enterprise, the enforcement provisions in Articles 17–24 bind you directly when competent authorities detect non-compliance.

todos.text: Set up a documented procedure to withdraw or recall any coffee, cocoa, or chocolate product immediately if competent authorities order it
todos.quote: withdrawing or recalling the relevant product immediately;

todos.text: Create a checklist to rectify formal non-compliance with Chapter 2 requirements (due diligence statements, geolocation data, risk assessments) within the period authorities specify
todos.quote: rectifying any formal non-compliance, in particular with the requirements of Chapter 2;

todos.text: Audit your due diligence system this month and fix any gaps — missing supplier geodata, incomplete risk mitigation, or undocumented verification steps — to prevent future non-compliance
todos.quote: the operator, downstream operator or trader shall address any shortcomings in the due diligence system with a view to preventing the risk of further non-compliance with this Regulation.

reasons: The obligations you were given are all addressed to EU Member States — they require France to lay down penalty rules, set fine levels, and notify the Commission.

Your shop is an operator that imports coffee, cocoa and chocolate from outside the EU and places them on the EU market, so the Deforestation Regulation applies to you, but Article 25 does not give you any direct duties; it binds France as a Member State, not you as a seller.
The quoted obligations are addressed to the Commission, competent authorities and customs authorities — not to operators or traders like your shop.

Your shop sells coffee, cocoa and chocolate (relevant products under the Regulation) and imports them from outside the EU, so the Regulation as a whole applies to you, but Article 27 itself imposes no duties on you as a seller.
The eight obligations you received are all addressed to the European Commission — they require the Commission to assign risk levels, classify countries, publish lists, and notify authorities.

Your shop sells coffee, cocoa and chocolate, which are covered by the Deforestation Regulation, but Article 29 itself imposes no duties on operators or traders; your obligations (due diligence, risk assessment) appear in other articles.
The quoted obligations are all addressed to the Commission and Member States, not to operators or traders like your shop.

Your shop sells coffee and cocoa (relevant products) and imports them from outside the EU, so you have obligations under other parts of the Deforestation Regulation, but Article 30 specifically tasks EU authorities with international cooperation, not individual businesses.
You sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate and import them from outside the EU, so the main regulation applies to you.

However, these specific articles (31 and 32) only impose duties on competent authorities and Member States — such as assessing concerns, informing submitters, protecting reporters' identities, and providing access to judicial review.
They do not create any new obligation for you as an operator or trader.
Therefore, this change does not require you to take any action.
Applies because you import coffee and cocoa from outside the EU, which are relevant products under the deforestation regulation.
As a medium-sized operator placing these products on the EU market, you must register in the Union information system and submit due diligence statements.
The information system is being set up by 30 December 2024, and your obligations take effect from that date.

todos.text: Register your company in the Union information system and include your EORI number in your registration profile
todos.quote: for operators placing relevant products under the customs procedure ‘release for free circulation’ or ‘export’, the Economic Operators Registration and Identification (EORI) number established pursuant to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 952/2013, shall be included in their registration profile

todos.text: Submit due diligence statements through the information system
todos.quote: registration of due diligence statements including the communication to the operator concerned of a reference number for each due diligence statement submitted through the information system

todos.text: Register as an operator in the Union information system
todos.quote: registration of operators and traders and their authorised representatives in the Union

reasons: The obligations you were given are addressed to the European Commission, not to sellers or operators.

Your shop sells coffee, cocoa and chocolate and imports them from outside the EU, so the Deforestation Regulation does apply to you in general, but Article 34 only requires the Commission to carry out reviews and report to the Parliament and Council.
No obligation in this article asks anything of a company that places those products on the EU market.
You sell coffee and cocoa, which are covered by the regulation, and you import them from outside the EU, so the regulation applies to your business.

However, the quoted obligations are all addressed to the Commission, the European Parliament, and the Council concerning the adoption and entry into force of delegated acts, not to operators placing products on the market.
This specific change therefore creates no direct obligations for your shop.
Your shop is established in France and ships to all 27 EU countries, so you sell to EU consumers.
You sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — physical goods — which the directive covers.
The directive applies to any business selling goods to EU consumers, and you import or make the goods yourself, placing them on the EU market.

todos.text: Add a clearly visible electronic withdrawal button or link to your storefront
todos.quote: you need to provide a clearly visible electronic withdrawal function, such as a button or link, that customers can use to exercise their withdrawal right directly from your store.

todos.text: Implement a two-step withdrawal confirmation where customers confirm and provide their name and order details
todos.quote: After a customer clicks a withdrawal button or link, they confirm the withdrawal and provide their name and the details of the contract or order they're canceling.

todos.text: Set up automatic email confirmation for withdrawal requests
todos.quote: Your store needs to send a confirmation of the withdrawal request to the customer on a durable medium, such as email.

reasons: This applies because you sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate to consumers in Germany (you ship to all 27 EU countries) and operate as an online B2C merchant.
The German law implementing the EU Consumer Rights Directive requires any trader targeting German consumers to provide an online withdrawal button and related processes.
Your company size (medium or large) and the fact that you import or produce the goods yourself mean you are the first to place them on the EU market, so the obligations bind you directly.

todos.text: Add a clearly labelled 'Vertrag widerrufen' button to your website
todos.quote: Online-Händler und Online-Dienstleister im B2C-Bereich müssen künftig auf ihren Internetseiten eine gut lesbare Schaltfläche mit der Aufschrift „Vertrag widerrufen“ oder einer gleichwertigen Formulierung bereitstellen.

todos.text: Ensure the cancellation button is easily findable, always visible during the withdrawal period, and works without registration
todos.quote: Die Schaltfläche muss ohne Weiteres zu finden und während der gesamten Widerrufsfrist gut sichtbar und durchgehend verfügbar sein – ohne Registrierung, Authentifizierung oder App-Download (außer, der Vertrag wurde über eine App geschlossen).

todos.text: Design the button accessibly with sufficient font size, contrast, and colour
todos.quote: Dabei sind auch die Anforderungen für Menschen mit Behinderungen nach dem Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz und der dazu ergangenen Verordnung zu beachten – wie etwa hinsichtlich Schriftgröße, Kontrast oder Schriftfarbe.

todos.text: Set up automatic email confirmation sent immediately when a consumer uses the withdrawal button
todos.quote: Nach Ausübung des Widerrufs muss der Unternehmer eine Eingangsbestätigung auf einem dauerhaften Datenträger (zum Beispiel per E-Mail) übermitteln.

todos.text: Update your withdrawal information to mention the online button and the confirmation email
todos.quote: Sie können Ihr Widerrufsrecht auch online unter (Internet-Adresse oder anderen geeigneten Hinweis, darüber eingeben, wo die Widerrufsfunktion verfügbar ist) ausüben. Wenn Sie diese Online-Funktion nutzen, übermitteln wir Ihnen auf einem dauerhaften Datenträger (z. B. durch eine E-Mail) unverzüglich eine Eingangsbestätigung mit Informationen zum Inhalt der Widerrufserklärung sowie dem Datum und der Uhrzeit ihres Eingangs.

todos.text: Update your privacy policy to cover data collected, processed, and stored via the withdrawal button
todos.quote: Auch die Datenschutzerklärung sollte angepasst werden – hinsichtlich der erhobenen Daten, deren Verarbeitung und Speicherdauer.

instrument: Directive (EU) 2024/825 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 28 February 2024 amending Directives 2005/29/EC and 2011/83/EU as regards empowering consumers for the green transition through better protection against unfair practices and through better information

reasons: We couldn't tell from your profile: whether harmonised EU requirements for reparability scores have been established for coffee, cocoa, or chocolate product groups. The obligation only applies when such requirements exist.
You are established in France, ship to all EU countries, and import or make your goods, so you are a trader placing products on the EU market.
The rule takes effect on 27 September 2026, but only for product groups with harmonised EU reparability requirements.

todos.text: Check whether harmonised EU reparability score requirements exist for your coffee, cocoa, and chocolate products
todos.quote: According to Articles 5(1)(i) and 6(1)(u) of the CRD, as amended by Article 2(2)(c), (3)(d) of the ECGT Directive, whenever harmonised EU requirements are established for a specific product or product group, traders must provide the reparability score to consumers in a clear and comprehensible manner before the consumer is bound by the contract.

reasons: You are established in France and ship to all 27 EU countries, so you direct your activities to consumers in the Union.
You sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate — consumer products that fall under the general product safety rules.
You import the goods from outside the EU or make them yourself, which makes you the economic operator placing them on the EU market.

todos.text: Verify that every coffee, cocoa, and chocolate product you list meets the EU general product safety requirements before you publish it
todos.quote: Economic operators shall place or make available on the market only safe products.

todos.text: Document which EU Member States your store targets through shipping zones, languages, and currencies to confirm the safety obligation applies to those markets
todos.quote: Products offered for sale online or through other means of distance sales shall be deemed to be made available on the market if the offer is targeted at consumers in the Union. An offer for sale shall be considered to be targeted at consumers in the Union if the relevant economic operator directs, by any means, its activities to one or more Member States.

reasons: applies because you are established in France, import coffee, cocoa and chocolate from outside the EU, and sell them to consumers across all 27 EU countries, making you an importer under the General Product Safety Regulation.
The regulation's importer duties took effect on 13 December 2024 and bind medium-sized or large enterprises like yours.

todos.text: Verify that each imported product meets the general safety requirement before you list it for sale
todos.quote: Before placing a product on the market, importers shall ensure that the product complies with the general safety requirement laid down in Article 5 and that the manufacturer has complied with the requirements set out in Article 9(2), (5) and (6).

todos.text: Register on the Safety Business Gateway and set up a process to immediately notify authorities and the manufacturer if a product is dangerous
todos.quote: Furthermore, where the product is a dangerous product, the importer shall immediately inform the manufacturer thereof and ensure that the market surveillance authorities are informed thereof through the Safety Business Gateway.

todos.text: Add your name, trade name, postal and electronic address, and single contact point address to product packaging or the product itself
todos.quote: Importers shall indicate their name, their registered trade name or registered trade mark, their postal and electronic address and, where different, the postal or electronic address of the single contact point at which they can be contacted.

todos.text: Ensure every product includes clear instructions and safety information in the language of each EU country you sell to
todos.quote: Importers shall ensure that the product they imported is accompanied by clear instructions and safety information in a language which can be easily understood by consumers, as determined by the Member State in which the product is made available on the market, except where the product can be used safely and as intended by the manufacturer without such instructions and safety information.

todos.text: Publish accessible communication channels on your storefront so consumers can submit complaints and report safety issues
todos.quote: Importers shall verify whether the communication channels referred to in Article 9(11) are publicly available to consumers, thereby allowing them to present complaints and communicate any accident or safety issue they have experienced with the product. If such channels are not available, importers shall provide for them, taking into account accessibility needs for persons with disabilities.

todos.text: Set up a register to log complaints, recalls and corrective measures for dangerous products and investigate each entry
todos.quote: Importers shall investigate complaints submitted, and information received on accidents, that concern the safety of products they made available on the market, which the complainant has alleged to be dangerous, and file those complaints, as well as product recalls and any corrective measures taken to bring the product into conformity, in the register referred to in Article 9(12), or in their own internal register.

reasons: You are established in France and ship to all 27 EU countries, so you operate inside the EU single market.
You sell coffee, cocoa and chocolate through a Shopify storefront, which counts as distance sales of consumer products.
You import those goods from outside the EU or make them yourself, so you are the importer or manufacturer placing them on the EU market.

The regulation binds manufacturers, importers, distributors and responsible persons for products sold at a distance, and its effective date of 13 December 2024 already applies to a medium-sized or large enterprise like yours.

todos.text: Add the manufacturer's name, trade name or trade mark, postal address and electronic contact details to every product page for distance sales
todos.quote: name, registered trade name or registered trade mark of the manufacturer, as well as the postal and electronic address at which they can be contacted

todos.text: Include a product picture, type designation and any other identifier on each distance-sales product page
todos.quote: information allowing the identification of the product, including a picture of it, its type and any other product identifier

todos.text: Display all required safety warnings and information in a language your customers can easily understand on the product, packaging or accompanying document
todos.quote: any warning or safety information to be affixed to the product or to the packaging or included in an accompanying document in accordance with this Regulation or the applicable Union harmonisation legislation in a language which can be easily understood by consumers

todos.text: Set up access to the Safety Business Gateway and notify any product-related accident to the competent authority of the Member State where it occurred without undue delay
todos.quote: The manufacturer shall ensure that, through the Safety Business Gateway, an accident caused by a product placed or made available on the market is notified, without undue delay from the moment it knows about the accident, to the competent authorities of the Member State where the accident has occurred

todos.text: If you learn of an accident involving a product you imported or distributed, inform the manufacturer without undue delay
todos.quote: The importers and the distributors which have knowledge of an accident caused by a product that they placed or made available on the market shall without undue delay inform the manufacturer thereof

todos.text: If the manufacturer is outside the EU, ensure the responsible person (which may be you) submits the accident notification via the Safety Business Gateway
todos.quote: Where the manufacturer of the product is not established in the Union, the responsible person within the meaning of Article 16(1) of this Regulation or Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 who has knowledge of an accident shall ensure that the notification is made

reasons: You are established in France and ship to all EU countries, so the EU packaging rules cover your shipments.
You import coffee, cocoa and chocolate from outside the EU or make them yourself, which makes you the economic operator placing those goods on the EU market and filling the packaging.

As a medium-sized or large enterprise you have no SME exemption, and the obligations address economic operators who fill e-commerce, transport, grouped or sales packaging — exactly what your Shopify store does when it ships orders.

todos.text: Measure and reduce empty space in your shipping boxes, grouped packaging and transport packaging to 50% or less
todos.quote: By 1 January 2030 or 3 years from the entry into force of the implementing acts adopted pursuant to paragraph 2, whichever is the latest, economic operators who fill grouped packaging, transport packaging or e-commerce packaging shall ensure that the maximum empty space ratio, expressed as a percentage, is 50 %.

todos.text: Reduce empty space in your product packaging to the minimum needed for protection and functionality
todos.quote: By 12 February 2028, the economic operators who fill sales packaging shall ensure that empty space is reduced to the minimum necessary for ensuring the packaging functionality, including product protection.

todos.text: Count filling materials such as bubble wrap, paper cuttings, air cushions and foam as empty space when you calculate packaging ratios
todos.quote: Space filled by filling materials, such as paper cuttings, air cushions, bubble wraps, sponge fillers, foam fillers, wood wool, polystyrene or Styrofoam chips, shall be considered as empty space.

reasons: Applies because you are established in France, ship to all 27 EU countries, and sell coffee, cocoa, and chocolate to end customers through your Shopify store.
The regulation requires EU merchants to display the official EU legal guarantee notice on every B2C sale, which covers your online shop.
It also requires the harmonised GARAN-Label for any free guarantees you offer that exceed two years.
As a medium-sized or large enterprise, the 27 September 2026 deadline applies to you.

todos.text: Add the official EU legal guarantee notice to your Shopify storefront for all consumer sales.
todos.quote: Ab dem 27. September 2026 muss bei **jedem Verkauf an Endkunden – also nicht im B2B Bereich** (sowohl im Online-Shop als auch am Point of Sale im Geschäft) gut sichtbar auf das gesetzliche Gewährleistungsrecht (Mängelhaftung von mindestens zwei Jahren) hingewiesen werden.

todos.text: If you offer any free guarantees longer than two years, add the harmonised GARAN-Label to those offers.
todos.quote: Die Angabe hat verpflichtend über das einheitliche [EU-Garantielabel (GARAN-Label)](https://europa.eu/youreurope/business/selling-in-eu/consumer-contracts-guarantees/eu-legal-guarantee-notice-and-garan-label/index_de.htm

reasons: You import coffee, cocoa and chocolate from outside the EU (or make them yourself), so you are the first to place their packaging on the EU market.
The regulation explicitly covers own brands and imports without a domestic intermediary, which matches your supply route.
You are established in France and ship to all 27 EU countries, putting you squarely inside the EU scope of the Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation.

todos.text: Register your business with the Central Packaging Register
todos.quote: Mit der Anwendung der EU-Verpackungsverordnung zum 12. August 2026 verschiebt sich die erweiterte Herstellerverantwortung für Verpackungen von Eigenmarken und Importen ohne inländischen Zwischenhändler grundlegend.

todos.text: Set up a process to report all packaging you place on the EU market to the Central Packaging Register
todos.quote: Mit der Anwendung der EU-Verpackungsverordnung zum 12. August 2026 verschiebt sich die erweiterte Herstellerverantwortung für Verpackungen von Eigenmarken und Importen ohne inländischen Zwischenhändler grundlegend.
